To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the C-terminal domain of WbaP is sufficient for catalysis, that the enzyme has high affinity for Und-P as the acceptor substrate and that it is highly efficient for the synthesis of the lipid-linked galactose-undecaprenyl phosphate intermediate.

the C-terminal domain of WbaP is sufficient for catalysis of the first reaction of O-antigens biosynthesis and that it is highly specific for Und-P. Bacterial surface glycan biosynthesis initiates with the transfer of a sugar-1-phosphate
the Wba-P C-terminal domain is sufficient to catalytically transfer Gal-1-phosphate from UDP-Gal to Und-P and that the Wba-PC-terminal domain is highly specific for Und-P.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and biochemical characterization of WbaP, a key enzyme in the biosynthesis of O-antigens of lipopolysacchardies.
the biochemical characterization of the C-terminal domain of WbaP.
the elucidation of the structure-function relationship of WbaP, a key enzyme for the biosynthesis of the bacterial surface polysaccharides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

WbaP is the prototype of a new family of membrane proteins that catalyzes the synthesis of Und-P-P-Gals, which are then transferred to acceptor oligosaccharides by glycosyltransferases to initiate the biosynthesis of surface glycans.
the WbaPC(CT) domain harbors the catalytic activity and substrate specificity for Und-P.
the C-terminal domain of WbaP is the minimal functional unit for the synthesis of the primers of the surface polysaccharide synthesis in bacteria.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WbaP, a membrane protein, has two catalytic domains, one in the N-terminal transmembrane domain and one in the cytoplasmic C-terminal domain.
the C-terminal domain of WbaP is sufficient for the catalytic activity and substrate specificity.
WbaP is composed of two domains, a catalytic C-terminal domain and an N-terminal domain with an essential role in membrane localization and stability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WbaP is an enzyme that catalyzes the synthesis of Und-P-P-Glycose and that the Wba(CT) domain harbors all the catalytic activity of the full-length WbaP.
the C-terminal domain of WbaP contains the catalytic site and is sufficient for catalysis.
WbaP contains a C-terminal catalytic domain that is sufficient to catalytically transfer Gal-1-phosphate from UDP-Gal to Und-P.
